findings.where: ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / getRecoveredAddress / revokeClaim (revocation keyed by raw signature bytes)
findings.why: Revocation stores the exact signature bytes, but getRecoveredAddress uses ecrecover without rejecting high-s or alternate-v signatures. The holder can submit a malleated version of the same signature, which recovers to the same signer but is not in revokedClaims. The holder's own identity key can then re-add it, so a revoked wallet becomes verified again and can receive tokens.
findings.steps: 1) Issuer calls revokeClaim for idB's original claim, which stores that signature as revoked. 2) b takes the original (r,s,v) and builds (r, n-s, v^1) with v flipped between 27 and 28. 3) b calls idB.addClaim(KYC_TOPIC, 1, claimIssuer, malleatedSig, data, ""), which passes isClaimValid. 4) ir.isVerified(b) is true again, so token.transfer or mint to b succeeds.

findings.where: MaxBalanceModule._getIdentity (used by moduleCheck, moduleTransferAction, moduleMintAction, moduleBurnAction)
findings.why: _getIdentity returns the wallet address and never looks up the identity in the registry. Wallets a1 and a2 both belong to idA but are tracked and capped separately, so the identity does not share one cap.
findings.steps: setUp as given (a1 and a2 both registered to idA, cap 1000). Agent mints 1000 to a1, then mints 1000 to a2. Both calls pass moduleCheck, because each wallet's own balance is counted. idA now holds 2000.

findings.why: The override mints 800 tokens to b before the MaxBalance module is bound, then presets idB's recorded balance to 0. The module's record for idB (0) no longer matches b's real balance (800). Any later transfer or mint to idB is therefore checked against the wrong balance. Any transfer out of b will revert on an underflow in moduleTransferAction, so those 800 tokens are stuck.
findings.steps: Setup: mint(b,800) with no modules bound; batchPreSetModuleState(idB,0); addModule(maxBalance). Then agent mints 1000 to b (or a funded holder transfers 1000 to b): moduleCheck sees 0+1000 <= 1000 and passes, so b holds 1800. b.transfer(x) reverts because _IDBalance[idB] (0) minus x underflows.

findings.where: Deployment._addModules (preset balance for idB set to 0 while b really holds 800)
findings.why: Because the module believes idB holds 0, it allows idB to receive up to 1000 more tokens on top of the real 800. b can end up with 1800, above the cap of 1000.
findings.steps: Setup as above. Then mint(b,1000), or transfer 1000 tokens from another verified holder to b. moduleCheck and moduleMintAction/moduleTransferAction both pass, and b's real balance is 1800.

findings.why: forcedTransfer calls _transfer but never calls _tokenCompliance.transferred. MaxBalanceModule's _IDBalance is therefore not updated, so the receiver's recorded balance stays too low and the sender's stays too high. The same gap affects recoveryAddress, which relies on forcedTransfer.
findings.steps: 1. Mint 900 to a wallet of identity B (b), so the module records 900 for idB. 2. Agent calls forcedTransfer(b, a1, 900); the real balance moves but the module still records idB=900 and idA=0. 3. Mint 1000 to a1 (check passes since idA is recorded at 0); a1 now really holds 1900, above the cap of 1000, so H1 is also broken. 4. Alternatively, b now holds 0 but the module still counts 900 for idB, so b is wrongly blocked from receiving more than 100.
